sentences.text: Shri V.P. Khare, learned counsel for the respondent No.3   ORDER 1 .

The appellants have filed this appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, being aggrieved by the award dated 20/3/2018 passed the 2nd Addl. Member MACT, Jhabua in Claim Case No.151/2017 challenging the adequacy of compensation.
2 . The factum of accident and liability of Insurance Company are not in dispute.
3 . The short facts giving rise to the case are that on 17/1/2016, deceased Bheriya @ Bheru went to Jaamkudi to attend the marriage ceremony.

At around 9.00 PM when they were returning and reached near Jhiri Sadava Road, the respondent No.1 came driving tractor bearing registration No.
M.P. 45 AA 3298 in a rash and negligent manner and rammed into the tempo of deceased because of which Bheriya @ Bheru sustained several grievous injuries on his head, legs and other parts of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:17062 2 MA-3241-2018 body.
He was brought to the primary health centre Kali Devi where he has died due to the injuries.
The appellants filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the death of the aforesaid person due to the accident.
The claims tribunal after considering the evidence brought on record concluded that the appellants are entitled for a total compensation of Rs.8,26,000/-.
4. Counsel for the appellants submits that the assessment of income of the deceased was not correct.

He refers to para 15 of the impugned award and submits that the appellants have examined contractor Rajbir Kushwah (AW.3) and produced certificate Exhibit P/5 who certifies that deceased was working as a mason and earning Rs.500/- per day.

The learned claims tribunal has disbelieved the statement of the said witness and has also repelled the above said certificate by observing that the contractor has not brought his registration number.
He has not brought any document to show that he is working as a contractor.

No document regarding construction, contract, tender etc were Smt. Manju vs Banshidhar on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136925433/
1 produced by him.

sentences.text: Thus the income of the deceased was taken on notional basis by treating him unskilled labourer at Rs.6000/- per month.
He submits that from the findings of para 15 itself it can be seen that the claims tribunal has accepted that the deceased was working as a mason.

Thus atleast he should have been treated as a semi skilled labourer and at the time of accident ie.,
17/1/2016 minimum wages for semi skilled labourer were Rs.7472/-.
He also submits that in terms of the schedule provided in the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, multiplier of 15 should have been applied as the deceased was 45 years of age.

He also submits that the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:17062 3 MA-3241-2018 dependency of the deceased was taken at 1/4th whereas there were nine members dependants.

He submits that the dependency has been taken for six dependants only for the reason that appellants / claimants No.6 to 8 were daughters who got married but he points out that the marriages were solemnized only after the death of the deceased.
At the time of accident all were unmarried and were dependent on the deceased.
Thus he submits that deduction under the head of personal expenses should have been made 1/6th of the income.

He also submits that no future prospects have been awarded which is contrary to the law as laid down by the Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others 2017 (16) SCC 680.

sentences.text: It is hence submitted that the amount awarded to the appellants be enhanced appropriately.
5. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent No.3 / Insurance Company submits that the findings of the award are correct and proper.

The contractor who came for proving the income of the deceased was only a witness brought by the claimants as he was not having any document so as to establish in the first place that he was a contractor.
Thus his statement that the deceased was working as a mason and earning Rs.500/- per day is doubtful and not trustworthy at all.
He further submits that the certificate issued by the said person cannot be relied upon.
Thus the claims tribunal has correctly taken the income of the deceased as Rs.6000/- per month on notional basis.

He further submits that the dependency at 1/4th is correct in view of the fact that there were six dependants in the considered view of the claims tribunal and married daughters no longer can be treated as dependant of deceased.
He also submits that at the time of accident the judgment of Pranay Sethi (supra) was not there.

Thus no future prospects could NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:17062 4 MA-3241-2018 have been provided by the claims tribunal.
Thus he supports the award.

6. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
7.

From a perusal of the findings recorded in para 13 to 15 of the impugned award, it can be seen that though the claims tribunal has discarded the assertion that the deceased was earning Rs.500/-
per day but it has been accepted in the last lines of para 15 of the impugned award that the deceased was working as a mason.
Thus even when the income of the deceased was being taken on notional basis, he should have been treated as a semi skilled labourer.
As per the guidelines issued by the State Legal Services Authority, the minimum wages for a semi skilled worker at the time of accident were Rs.7472/- per month.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Hans Raj V/s. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Anr by order dated 20/8/2024 has held in para 5 and 6 as under :-
"5.

entities.text: Hans Raj V/s. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Having considered the submissions and looking at the findings recorded by the High Court, it is required to be observed that the guidelines issued from time to time by the State Legal Services Authority were to ordinarily apply where the proof of earning is not available and to settle such disputes in Lok Adalat.

It is also required to be observed that such guidelines ought not to be made applicable for determining just and reasonable compensation in the cases where the proof of earning has been brought on record.

In the facts of this case, we have no hesitation to conclude that the High Court had misdirected itself while reducing the amount of compensation relying upon the guidelines of Rajasthan State Legal Services Authority, which were not binding on them.

6. In view of the foregoing, it is to conclude that henceforth, the guidelines, if any,
issued by any of the State Legal Services Authority of the High Court would apply as guiding factor in the cases where the proof of income is not available and ordinarily to decide the cases in Lok Adalat.
Such guidelines are not binding either on the High Court or on MACT to determine just and fair compensation.
The Courts are at liberty to decide the amount of compensation while appreciating the evidence so brought on record and what is just and reasonable in the facts.

In absence of such evidence, the guidelines of the legal services authority may be relied upon but only for guidance."
9.

Thus in absence of any document to prove the income of the deceased and NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:17062 5 MA-3241-2018 in view of the fact that he has been treated as mason by the claims tribunal, the income of the deceased is taken at Rs.7472/- by considering him the semi-skilled labourer.
10. As regards the multiplier it is seen from the findings in para 13 of the award that the deceased was 45 years.

Thus in view of the law as laid down by the Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma &
Ors. V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. , AIR 2009 SC 3140 the correct multiplier of 14 has been applied by the claims tribunal.

sentences.text: 11. As regards the contention of the appellants that the dependency at 1/4th is not correct in view of the fact that there were nine dependants, it is to be seen that at the time of accident all nine were dependant on the deceased but subsequently three of them got married.

Thus in the considered view of this Court depedency should be taken at 1/5th.
12.

It is also seen that nothing has been added for future prospects, in view of the law as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex court in the case of Pranay Sethi (supra), the future prospects has to be awarded.
In the present case the deceased was a mason of the age of 45 years.
Thus 25% has to be added for future prospects in the income of the deceased.
After the modification of the income and addition of future prospects and the modification in the personal expenses the just and proper compensation now would come to 12,48,576/-.

sentences.text:
However, it is seen from the findings in para 19 that the claims tribunal has awarded only an amount of Rs.40,000/- under the head of consortium although there are 9 claimants who are wife,
widow of deceased, children and father of the deceased.

Nothing has been awarded in this head to other claimants although they are either father or son / daughters of the deceased who are also entitled for payment of compensation for loss of consortium in view of the law as laid down NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:17062 6 MA-3241-2018 by the Apex Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Nanu Ram, 2019 ACJ SC 2782 .

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Nanu Ram, 2019 ACJ SC 2782
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
As such for each of the claimants an amount of Rs.40,000/- is awarded, the total of which comes to Rs.3,60,000/-.
14.
The appellants are also entitled for Rs.15,000/- for loss of estate and Rs.15,000/- for loss of funeral expenses.

After adding the enhanced amount by this Court on the other heads as aforestated,
the appellants are now held entitled to receive a sum of Rs.16,38,576/-.
However, the claims tribunal has already awarded Rs.8,26,000/- to the appellants.

Thus now after deducting the amount awarded by the claims tribunal from the amount enhanced by this Court, the appellants are now held entitled to receive a sum of Rs.8,12,576/-, which shall be paid to the appellants by the respondent No.3/ Insurance Company over and above what has already been awarded by the claims tribunal.
The enhanced amount shall carry the interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of application.
Rest of the conditions of the award shall remain intact.
15. As the appellant has valued this appeal at Rs.6,00,000/- he has to pay deficit Court fees within a period of one month from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
16. Accordingly, the appeal is partly allowed and disposed of in above terms.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE SS/-
